verdicts.quote: "To align with OAuth 2.0 security best practices, we have introduced two new v3 OAuth API endpoints."
verdicts.reason: HubSpot’s own changelog documents OAuth 2.x token endpoints for apps; for multi‑tenant customer installs, OAuth is the primary method despite account‑level Service Keys existing.

verdicts.quote: "Do I need a paid HubSpot account to develop? No. You can create a free HubSpot account and build apps without a paid subscription."
verdicts.reason: HubSpot states you can self‑serve a free developer account (with test accounts), which yields working app credentials; marketplace review is for listings, not to obtain creds.
HubSpot’s release notes enumerate many CRM and non‑CRM API families (contacts, deals, tickets, files, campaigns, sequences, pipelines, etc.), indicating broad coverage across the product.

verdicts.quote: "The HubSpot MCP server connects any MCP-compatible AI tool to your CRM over a secure, HubSpot-hosted connection authenticated via OAuth 2.1 with PKCE."
verdicts.reason: This is an official, vendor‑hosted MCP server, not a community project.

verdicts.quote: "HubSpot's comprehensive API library and developer-friendly architecture lets your team build deeper, customized connections."
verdicts.reason: Free, self‑serve creds plus extensive, versioned REST APIs and an official MCP server mean an agent toolkit can be shipped now; app listing review is optional for Marketplace exposure, not a blocker.
